body.en: A function assigns exactly one output to each input. The EST I tests function notation, composition, inverses, and transformations.

Notation: \( f(x) \) means the output of \( f \) at input \( x \). Composition: \( (f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x)) \). Inverse: \( f^{-1} \) reverses \( f \); find it by swapping \( x \) and \( y \) and solving for \( y \). Transformation: \( f(x)+k \) shifts up, \( f(x-h) \) shifts right, \( -f(x) \) reflects over \( x \)-axis.

Domain and range

The domain is all valid inputs; the range is all possible outputs. For \( f(x)=\sqrt{x-3} \), the domain is \( x\geq 3 \) (argument under the root must be non-negative). For \( f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x-2} \), exclude \( x=2 \) from the domain.

figure.title: Function Transformation: f(x) = x² and g(x) = (x - 2)² - 3

caption.en: Transformation of the parent function \(f(x) = x^2\) (blue) into \(g(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 3\) (coral), representing a horizontal shift of 2 units right and vertical shift of 3 units down to vertex \((2, -3)\).

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Functions & Graphs

body.en:
• Horizontal Shift Reversal: The transformation \(f(x - h)\) shifts the graph to the RIGHT by \(h\), while \(f(x + h)\) shifts the graph to the LEFT by \(h\). The sign inside the parentheses always behaves counter-intuitively.
  • Composition Evaluation Order: For \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\), always calculate the inner function \(g(x)\) first, then feed the result into the outer function \(f\). In general, \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\).
  • Finding Inverses: To find \(f^{-1}(x)\), replace \(f(x)\) with \(y\), swap \(x\) and \(y\), and solve for \(y\). The domain of \(f\) becomes the range of \(f^{-1}\), and the range of \(f\) becomes the domain of \(f^{-1}\).
  • Function Identification (Vertical Line Test): A relation is a function if and only if each input \(x\) has at most one output \(y\). If a vertical line intersects the curve more than once (like a circle or sideways parabola), it is NOT a function.

question.en: The graph of \(y = f(x)\) is shifted 3 units right and reflected in the \(x\)-axis. Write the new equation in terms of \(f\).
Let \(f(x) = 3x - 4\) and \(g(x) = x^2 + 1\). (a) Evaluate \((g \circ f)(2)\). (b) Determine the value of \(x\) such that \(f^{-1}(x) = 5\).

solution.en:
(a) Composition \(g(f(2))\): First evaluate the inner function: \[ f(2) = 3(2) - 4 = 6 - 4 = 2. \] Now substitute into \(g\): \[ g(2) = (2)^2 + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5. \]

(b) Inverse evaluation: By definition, \(f^{-1}(x) = 5 \iff f(5) = x\). Compute \(f(5)\): \[ x = f(5) = 3(5) - 4 = 15 - 4 = 11. \] Thus \(x = 11\).
